audit.whatIsWrong: Content win[] and the full-layer phases both read Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Skill / Skill / Graves, while the packet levelChart reads Neeko / Skill / Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Skill. The two charts are wrong at five of seven rows — and in the same rows in both layers.
audit.why: The content whys already describe the packet order precisely: whys[0] 'at level 1 you're stuck eating it, so just farm and don't trade' is a Neeko row, whys[1] 'roughly even' is Skill, whys[4] 'you beat her at 6' and whys[5] 'your peak' are Graves rows, and whys[6] 'makes the late game skill-dependent' is Skill. The enums were never updated to match the prose.
audit.corrected: Both charts set to Neeko / Skill / Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Skill, ratings 4,5,7,7,7,7,5 from the Graves side.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer marks Level 6 and first item as 'Skill' at 4/10, its weakest rows, and describes them with generic Graves boilerplate. Both are Graves' strongest stages here.
audit.why: Pop Blossom is 120/105/90s with a visible preparation before the leap, and Quickdraw's 16/15/14/13/12s dash clears it — so Level 6 favours Graves rather than flipping the lane. The first item is Graves' peak because Neeko is a squishy pick-mage whose only outs are Shapesplitter's clone-and-speed and the Tangle-Barbs root, neither of which is a dash.
audit.corrected: phases[4] and [5] flipped to Graves at 7/10 and rewritten to name the actual spike reasons.
sources: enemyKit R cd 120/105/90 and Riot text
enemyKit W Riot text (clone plus move speed, no dash)

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated ability names: whys[5] and spikes[2].text both credit 'Bushwhack armor from E'. Graves has no ability called Bushwhack.
audit.why: Riot's text for Graves' E is Quickdraw — 'Graves dashes forward gaining an Armor and Magic Resist boost... gain two stacks of True Grit'. The resist buff is True Grit, the dash is Quickdraw. Bushwhack belongs to a different champion entirely, and it appears twice in this matchup's copy.
audit.corrected: Both instances replaced with True Grit stacks from Quickdraw.

audit.whatIsWrong: content mid says 'W's blind doesn't cancel the stun'; spikes[3].text says 'her W smoke cuts her vision but its blind won't stop the R cast'; report[10].t says 'W smoke blinds tower dives'; phases[6].why says 'smoke-screen blinds'.
audit.why: Graves' Smoke Screen is not a blind — Riot: 'creating a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range. Enemies caught in the initial impact are dealt magic damage and have their Move Speed reduced briefly.' The spikes[3] line is doubly wrong: it attributes the smoke to Neeko ('her W smoke') when Shapesplitter is a clone and a move-speed buff, and Smoke Screen is Graves' own W.
audit.corrected: Every reference rewritten as reducing sight range and slowing on impact, and the smoke reattributed to Graves.
sources: ownerKit W Riot text and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states Tangle-Barbs' range or what happens when it passes through something first.
audit.why: Riot: 'Neeko slings a tangle that damages and roots everything it passes through. If the tangle kills an enemy or passes through a champion, it becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer.' At 1000 range with a 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s cooldown, that is the ability that beats Graves before Quickdraw exists — and a tangle that clips a minion-line champion first is a longer root, which is exactly why standing behind the wave is not automatic safety here.
audit.corrected: Range and cooldown put into enemyWin and dosFull[2].d.
sources: enemyKit E Riot text, range 1000, cd 12/11.5/11/10.5/10

edits.before: This is your window. Through 4-5 your stacking armor/MR and E charges compound, and a pre-6 Neeko has nothing that survives an E-in, Q-cone, auto, auto sequence — she's a pick-mage, not a duelist. At 6 respect Pop Blossom (R): the expanding ring around her during the channel is the tell, so the instant you see it, dash clear with E or drop W smoke on her to slow and shrink her vision before she leaps. Note her R is an ability, so W's blind doesn't cancel the stun — the value is the slow and vision-cut, not the blind. The moment her R or E is on cooldown, walk her down; she has no way to kite a Graves sitting on two Quickdraw charges.
edits.after: This is your window. Through 4-5 your True Grit stacks and E charges compound, and a pre-6 Neeko has nothing that survives an E-in, Q-cone, auto, auto sequence — she's a pick-mage, not a duelist. At 6 respect Pop Blossom (R): the ring around her during the preparation is the tell, so the instant you see it, dash clear with E or drop W smoke on her to slow and shrink her vision before she leaps. Smoke Screen is not a blind — it reduces sight range and slows on impact, so it never cancels the cast. The moment her 90-second R or her E is down, walk her down; she cannot kite a Graves sitting on two Quickdraw charges.

notes: Two fabricated ability names found and killed: 'Bushwhack armor from E' appeared in BOTH whys[5] and spikes[2].text — Graves' E is Quickdraw and the resist buff is True Grit; Bushwhack is not a Graves ability at all. spikes[3].text also mis-attributed Graves' Smoke Screen to Neeko ('her W smoke') when Shapesplitter is a clone plus a move-speed buff, and then claimed a blind that does not exist on either champion. Smoke Screen was called a blind in four separate places in this matchup; all corrected to 'reduces sight range and slows on impact' per Riot's text. Level chart was wrong at five of seven rows in BOTH layers while the content whys had it right — proposed as one atomic group in each layer. I left diff at EVEN and difficulty 5.5/10 rather than upgrading them: the chart and the 55.56% win rate both lean Graves, but the sample is only 18 games, so a difficulty re-rating on that basis would be a guess. Flagged for the user rather than changed. Kit flag caution: the derived flags again claim Graves' Q 'creates terrain' — Riot's text says only that it detonates on colliding with terrain, so I removed the 'wall-bounce' framing from phases[2] instead of repeating it. Mirror file neeko__graves did not exist at audit time.
